why: issue 1589 -- PRESENT since then, same name and signature (`bool rcl_logging_rosout_enabled(void)`, `<rclc/rosout.h>`), and it answers upstream's build-time question: true iff the image was built with the `rosout` capability. ADOPT for the function itself -- its contract is upstream's exactly. Since phase-556 W13 the runtime republishes as upstream does: the executor creates one `/rosout` publisher per node in its table and pumps the record queue from every spin, with no user action (a legacy C `rclc_node_init_default` node is not in that table and keeps the explicit `rclc_rosout_*` spelling). What still differs, and why the row stays a divergence: that publisher is VOLATILE (`nros_node::rosout::qos_bounded`), where upstream's is TRANSIENT_LOCAL KEEP_LAST(1000) (user ruling 2026-11-13), so a tool that subscribes after boot misses the boot records; and it is switched per IMAGE (the `rosout` capability, or the stock node interfaces), not per node. It is a declared entity: the inventory prices one publisher per node from the capability. Which records reach the topic follows the ROS release (RFC-0102 D4). Measured against a stock `ros2 topic echo /rosout` by interop cells `native-logging-{rust,c,cpp}-zenoh-n2r` (`packages/testing/nros-tests/tests/rosout_interop.rs`). History: until issue 1589 this row was `divergence`+`absent` -- the topic existed only in Rust; until phase-556 W13 the application created the publisher and pumped it.
